€6 MILLION allocated to new Fire Stations for West Wicklow 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the announcement of funding for two new fire stations to be built in 
Dunlavin and Baltinglass under the Government’s new multimillion Fire Services Capital Programme. 
This represents a combined investment of €6 million for the two fire stations. 
In addition, Wicklow has been allocated two new fire appliances to maintain and improve the quality of 
the fleet. 
FUNDING OF NEARLY €170,000 ALLOCATED FOR WICKLOW’S HISTORIC BUILDINGS 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the recent announcement of capital funding for two properties in 
County Wicklow under the Historic Structures Fund (HSF). 
The HSF scheme is co-ordinated by Wicklow County Council on behalf of the Department of Housing, 
Local Government and Heritage. The core aims of this fund are to enable larger scale conservation works 
to be carried out on historic structures which are deemed to be significant and in need of urgent 
support, encourage the regeneration and reuse of historic structures, and to support the conservation 
of historic structures for community benefit. 
HSF funded works promote the use of traditional materials and craft skills, supporting employment in 
specialist conservation trades and aligning fully with the aims of the scheme to enable larger-scale 
conservation, sustain heritage skills, and build climate resilience in historic structures. 
Funding boost of over €500,000 for Archaeological Monuments in County Wicklow  
Wicklow County Council welcomes the recent announcement of €544,415 in funding for archaeological 
monuments in County Wicklow through the Community Monuments Fund 2026. 
The Community Monuments Fund (CMF) aims to conserve, protect and promote monuments and 
historic sites, encouraging access and making them more climate resilient through supporting essential 
repairs.

Energy Retrofit Program 
As part of our ongoing Energy Efficiency retrofit programme, housing services are undertaking works across 
the county. This includes, depending on house surveyed, and not limited to external wall insulation, attic 
insulation, heat pumps and upgraded windows and doors. These works comply with our policy on energy 
fabric upgrades which went through the SPC in 2023. 
The driver of this programme is the improvement to energy efficiency of local authority properties (BER – 
B2 or better), energy cost savings and sustainability. The move from solid fuel to more sustainable, energy 
efficient and cost-effective heating systems contributes to the climate change agenda and dramatically 
improves the comfort levels of tenants in these properties.

The Homeless HAP Place finder provides assistance in: 
• 
seeking out potential properties suitable for households currently identified as homeless or at risk 
of homelessness. 
• 
liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs. 
• 
establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and, 
• 
supporting those homeless households to (a) prevent the necessity to enter emergency 
accommodation or (b) to exit emergency accommodation and secure a tenancy. 
• 
To date, 694 households (484 families & 208 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless 
HAP Scheme in Wicklow County Council from the inception on 1st October 2018 to 31st March 
2026. (268 homeless cases, 379 prevention cases to date and 48 direct provision).  175 
properties were sourced by WCC. 
 
Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 10 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units.  
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.

Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support 
needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved 
into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful. 
Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East 
Region. Wicklow County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed 
the targets identified in the programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis for 
recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the implementation 
of the programme. 
Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 19 clients under Housing First.  Other 
clients proposed for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key support work 
pending finalisation of sourcing of accommodation. The main issue facing this programme is the availability 
of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy access to required services.

Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026 
This funding will provide capital supports that are essential for many small community groups and 
organisations, particularly those who serve disadvantaged communities in rural and urban areas. 
The scheme is designed to ensure local priorities are identified and met, to improve and enhance 
community facilities for all. Funding will be available to a diverse range of community groups including, but 
not limited to, community centres, parish halls and local voluntary groups. 
County Wicklow has received €199,043.66 as part of the Local Enhancement Programme 2026. 
The Wicklow Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) is responsible for allocating funding 
through this scheme. Applications must relate to one or more key priority areas identified in their LCDC's 
Local Economic and Community Plan (LECP) to be eligible for consideration. 
Applications are now closed expecting announcement from the Department of Rural and Community 
Development and the Gaeltacht June 2026.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant 
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Offer a Home programme 
The 'Offer a Home' programme is being managed by local authorities on behalf of Government. Rent is not payable to 
homeowners as they are offering the property but a tax-free payment, Accommodation Recognition Payment (ARP), of 
€600 per month per property is available through the Government's Recognition Payment Scheme, managed by the 
Department of Social Protection. 
Changes to the eligibility criteria for the Accommodation Recognition Payment (ARP) have been introduced under Part 
3 of the Residential Tenancies (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026. 
From 3 March 2026, new applications for properties that have been registered with the Residential Tenancies Board 
(RTB) will no longer meet the scheme’s eligibility criteria. This applies to properties registered with the RTB at any time 
since 4 March 2022. Tenants in rental properties will also no longer be eligible to make new applications for the 
scheme. 
The Government has extended the ARP to 31 March 2027, in line with the EU Temporary Protection Directive.

Transport & Infrastructure and Sustainable Communities 
Work has been completed on a Sustainable Communities Report to support housing proposals in 
Newtownmountkennedy. This report assesses the availability of key local services, including education, healthcare, 
transport, and recreational facilities. It provides an evidence-based overview to ensure new developments are 
supported by appropriate infrastructure.  
Planning Data and MyPlan Submissions 
Significant progress has been made in preparing planning data for submission to the Department’s MyPlan system. This 
included improving the accuracy of zoning maps and updating spatial data to support Local Area Plans in Wicklow 
Town–Rathnew, Greystones–Delgany, and Kilcoole. These updates are important to ensure consistency and 
transparency in the statutory planning process.  
Call for Sites and Public Mapping Tools 
A number of digital tools have been developed to support the Call for Sites process. This includes both an internal 
assessment portal and a public-facing map viewer, which will be launched following data preparation. Enhancements to 
mapping data and analysis tools have improved how sites are assessed against environmental and zoning criteria.  
Environmental Mapping and Biodiversity Projects 
Work has commenced on a new interactive mapping project focused on swift bird populations. Data has been received 
and is currently being processed, including information on nest box locations. This project will support biodiversity 
awareness and conservation efforts. It builds on existing environmental mapping initiatives and will be made available to 
the public. 
Electoral Areas, Data Sharing and Support Services 
Progress has been made in updating polling district information, including the identification of additional polling stations 
and preparation of supporting maps. The team also facilitated external data requests, including supporting a Town 
Centre Health Check for Carnew and Wicklow Town.  
Systems Development and Operational Support 
A wide range of systems and applications have been maintained and enhanced to support Council operations. This 
includes new tools for housing, enforcement, finance, and broadband planning, as well as continued development of 
modern GIS web applications. Staff training and user support have been provided to ensure effective use of these 
systems
